source.title: Video Pose Distillation for Few-Shot, Fine-Grained Sports Action Recognition
source.authors: James Hong; Matthew Fisher; Michaël Gharbi; Kayvon Fatahalian

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present. Some table text is flattened, but the results used below can be assigned from the table layout.
record.tranche_reason: It tests a teacher-to-student distillation approach in vision, a modality named by V6, and reports downstream results against teacher-feature baselines. It is a new setting and does not reproduce the original weak-to-strong task or measure PGR.
record.gate_note: The student is trained to regress pose features from an off-the-shelf pose teacher, then evaluated through downstream sports tasks against features from that teacher. It is not a test of a strong pretrained model fine-tuned on task labels from a weaker supervisor, and the paper does not report PGR. The action-retrieval table reports teacher/student comparisons, but its flattened layout does not permit reliable assignment of the individual values to models and cutoffs.
record.test_reason: This 2021 paper predates and does not cite the weak-to-strong work, so it does not test the claim. A randomly initialised ResNet-34 student regresses an off-the-shelf pose teacher's features, using extra optical-flow input. The study then compares the two feature sets on downstream sports tasks. There is no pretrained strong student, no task labels from a weaker supervisor, no strong ceiling and no PGR. 'Student features beat teacher features downstream' is a related distillation construct, not V1 or V6 as defined. It is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude VPD improves pose-feature reliability and downstream accuracy in label-poor sports video, especially where pose is unreliable (FX35, Diving48). They report only slight gains over VIPE* on FSJump6 and Tennis7, and say VPD stays competitive or state-of-the-art with full data, except Diving48, where GSM is better.
record.recipe_differences: The student is randomly initialized and trained to regress machine-generated pose features (including temporal derivatives) from video; the study evaluates those features on downstream sports tasks. It does not fine-tune a strong pretrained model on task labels from a weaker task supervisor or calculate PGR.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies by dataset and training-data amount. The paper reports that action-only distillation performs worse than distillation on uncut video; pose-confidence selection thresholds also affect performance, with overly high thresholds reducing it.

fits_no_version.finding: A randomly initialised ResNet-34 student distilled from a pose teacher's features, with added RGB and optical-flow input, yields features that beat the teacher's features on downstream sports tasks. This holds in most settings: up to +22.8 points on few-shot Diving48, and higher detection AP. In 16-shot FSJump6 the two are within noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Student-surpasses-teacher in feature distillation for vision (noisy-student-style), measured on downstream tasks rather than PGR.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV), 2021
record.problems: The evidence is a vision-specific feature-distillation setup rather than the weak-to-strong task-label fine-tuning claim. The student is randomly initialized, no strong-model ceiling or PGR is measured, and the downstream comparisons do not establish the original claim's mechanism. The paper reports means over sampled subsets in some experiments, but the selected Table 2(a) and Table 4 comparisons give no uncertainty values.
record.rows_left_out: The individual action-retrieval values in Table 3 were not extracted because the supplied flattened table layout does not permit reliable assignment of values to feature types, datasets, and cutoffs. The paper describes VPD as outperforming teacher features at all reported cutoffs and datasets.

untested.parts: No strong pretrained student, no weak task-label supervision, no strong ceiling, no PGR.
None of the named weak-to-strong training changes are tested.
No variation in model size or PGR.
The vision weak-to-strong setup (pretrained strong student on weak labels, PGR) is not tested.

missing.what: Retrieval precision@k for teacher vs VPD features. The table is legible in the text: e.g. Diving48 P@1 is 34.5 (2D joints) vs 64.4 (2D-VPD), and 36.1 (VIPE*) vs 60.9 (VI-VPD).
Means ±SD over five few-shot subsets for teacher and VPD features at 4 to 32 shots.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T3/V6 'tests' classification is rejected. The study predates weak-to-strong and differs in the key respects: the student is randomly initialised rather than pretrained, it gets extra input (flow), and the outcome is downstream feature quality, not PGR. No verdicts are given. Several 'reversed' states (r10, r17, r18) are within reported noise and should be 'absent'. The ablation rows (r17–r30) are compared by the paper with uncut-video VPD, not with the teacher.

versions.untested_parts: No weak-to-strong task-label fine-tuning, supervisor task performance, strong-model ceiling, or PGR measurement.
The paper ablates VPD components, but does not test the named weak-to-strong training changes or compare their PGR with naive fine-tuning.
It does not measure PGR across model sizes, NLP/chess/reward modelling tasks, or predictors of weak-to-strong generalization.
It does not test weak-supervisor exploitability, weak-to-strong distribution-shift performance, or error-alignment effects.
No theoretical conditions for a student to beat its supervisor are tested or derived.
The study tests pose-feature distillation for sports video tasks, not other vision settings generally; it does not use a pretrained strong student, task labels from a weaker supervisor, or PGR.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Sports-video pose distillation; action recognition, with most tested recognition settings and both detection tasks
reader_labels.reason: VPD features exceed teacher-feature baselines in most reported settings, including the detection results (r1-r9, r11-r16, r19-r30, r31-r39). These are vision results, but not the original PGR test.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: VI-VPD on FSJump6 recognition, and action-only distillation on FSJump6
reader_labels.reason: The student does not exceed the teacher-feature baseline for 16-shot VI-VPD on FSJump6 or for either action-only FSJump6 result (r10, r17-r18); several other settings show only small gains (r9, r40).
